fundamentals.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Lumentum Holdings Inc. manufactures and sells optical and photonic products in the Americas, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. It operates through two segments, Cloud & Networking and Industrial Tech. The Cloud & Networking segment offers optical and photonic chips, components, modules, and subsystems supplied to cloud data center operators, AI/ML infrastructure providers, and network equipment manufacturer customers that are building cloud data centers and network infrastructures. Its Industrial Tech segment provides short-pulse solid-state lasers, kilowatt-class fiber lasers, diode lasers, and gas lasers that serves the semiconductor device, solar cell, display, and electric vehicle and battery manufacturing markets. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

judgment.summary: Lumentum is a high-growth company with strong margins and analyst backing, though its valuation is high and leverage is notable.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat estimates with EPS of 2.37 vs 2.27; next earnings date is 2026-08-12.
positives: Revenue growth 90.1% YoY and analyst estimates of 236.6% for the current quarter and 300.7% for the current fiscal year indicate massive expansion.
Operating margin of 21.8% and profit margin of 17.7% demonstrate strong profitability.
Return on equity at 22.8% is robust.
The PEG ratio of 0.63 suggests the stock may be undervalued relative to its growth prospects.
24 analysts have a consensus 'buy' rating with a mean target of $1113.01.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 153.94 and Forward P/E of 48.65 indicate a very high valuation.
Price/Book of 74.26 and Price/Sales of 27.53 also suggest a premium valuation.
Debt/Equity ratio of 111.44 indicates significant leverage.
Free cash flow of $93.35M TTM is modest relative to market cap.
A report on CPO rollout delay could pose a risk to future growth.

news.paragraph: Lumentum (LITE) saw its stock climb 5% on Tuesday, riding the AI boom alongside other optics stocks, according to Yahoo Finance. This follows a Barron's report suggesting it's time to buy the dip in both LITE and Coherent, despite recent stock price declines. However, a Seeking Alpha article from June 10th noted a potential delay in the CPO rollout, which could impact networking stocks, creating a mixed sentiment around the name.
